provenance.sourceName: ACME Electronics material workbook "16-A043.xlsx" (archive "20250522 Material A2 for Wurth.7z", supplied by ACME to Wurth Elektronik)
provenance.verificationMethod: Sheet '3data', columns 'Freq(KHz)' and 'loss factor(tanδ/μi)' in units of 1e-6; 544 of 544 rows kept, 0 rows at and above the first non-positive value dropped; 1e+03 Hz to 2.64e+06 Hz. Replaces a curve that was mu''/(mu' mu_i) computed from sheet 2data (the method of f29019d for the other ACME grades). ABT #2251: only the rows ACME publishes are kept: the workbook column is the curve of the 'Loss Factor V.S. Frequency' chart in ACME's catalogue (acme_product_now.pdf, pdf page 54, printed 52), which is drawn only up to 1000e-6 and 1e4 kHz. The 32 rows from 1685 kHz up lie outside that frame (they diverge to 1.82 towards the measurement's resonance) and are dropped; the stored curve now ends at 1660 kHz (0.00093).

provenance.sourceName: ACME Electronics, ferrite product catalogue, Material Characteristics-A043
provenance.verificationMethod: pdf page 54 (printed 52), table "Material Characteristics-A043" (toroid, 10 kHz, H as printed): Bs 460/300 mT at 25/100 C; Br 65/60 mT at 25/100 C; Tc ≥160 C (stored as the printed lower bound); resistivity 0.20 ohm m; density 4.85 g/cm3; mu_i 4500 ± 25% at 25 C (the stored mu_i(T) curve gives 4440 at 25 C); relative loss factor <10 at 10kHz, <10 at 100kHz x10^-6; listed under "Material Characteristics (Mn-Zn Ferrite)" in the summary tables (pdf page 16).
